articles.summary: A Chinese-speaking hacking group known as CL-STA-1062 has created and deployed a new backdoor tool called TinyRCT to attack government agencies and critical infrastructure operators in Southeast Asia. articles.title: New Linux pedit COW Exploit Enables Root Access by Poisoning Cached Binaries
articles.summary: A critical Linux kernel vulnerability called CVE-2026-46331, or 'pedit COW,' allows unprivileged local users to gain root-level access by exploiting a flaw in the traffic-control subsystem. This out-of-bounds write vulnerability corrupts shared memory pages used by the system, and a working exploit was publicly released within a day of the CVE announcement. The flaw poses an immediate risk to Linux systems that haven't been patched.
articles.whyItMatters: This vulnerability is critical because any local user can exploit it to gain full system control without special privileges, making it a severe risk for multi-user systems and shared hosting environments. articles.summary: Amazon Q Developer contained a high-severity vulnerability that allowed malicious repositories to execute commands and steal developer credentials through improper handling of Model Context Protocol servers. articles.title: Polymarket customers lose $3 million in supply-chain attack
articles.summary: Polymarket, a cryptocurrency prediction platform, suffered a supply-chain attack where hackers compromised a third-party vendor and injected malicious code into the platform's frontend. The attack resulted in approximately $3 million in customer losses, though the company committed to reimbursing affected users. This incident highlights how attackers can exploit trusted vendors to gain access to high-value targets.
articles.whyItMatters: Supply-chain attacks are particularly dangerous because they exploit trust relationships and can affect numerous organizations through a single compromised vendor. This incident demonstrates that even financial platforms with security measures remain vulnerable if their trusted partners are compromised, making vendor security assessment critical for risk management.

articles.whyItMatters: This attack demonstrates a critical vulnerability in AI-powered customer support systems that can be manipulated to bypass security controls, affecting even high-value government accounts. articles.title: Google Details Turla's New STOCKSTAY Backdoor Used in Ukraine Espionage Attacks
articles.summary: Google has identified a new .NET backdoor called STOCKSTAY deployed by the Russian state-sponsored group Turla against Ukrainian government and military targets, as well as organizations interested in Italian foreign policy. articles.title: WhatsApp VBScript Campaign Uses Fake Documents to Install ManageEngine RMM Tool
articles.summary: Cybercriminals are using WhatsApp to send fake documents disguised as legitimate files that actually contain malicious VBScript code. When users run these scripts, they unknowingly install ManageEngine RMM software, giving attackers remote access to their computers. This campaign is actively targeting WhatsApp Desktop and Web users across multiple countries including Malaysia, Brazil, India, and others.
articles.whyItMatters: This attack demonstrates how legitimate administrative tools can be weaponized when combined with social engineering through popular messaging platforms, making it difficult for users to distinguish dangerous files from safe ones. RMM software in attacker hands provides complete remote control over victim machines, enabling data theft, further malware deployment, and system compromise at scale.

articles.title: Anthropic is testing desktop-like Claude Cowork for mobile

articles.summary: Cybercriminals are exploiting Shopify's Shop order-tracking app by injecting fraudulent purchase receipts into users' accounts. articles.title: Chrome Ad Blocker with 10M+ Installs Found with Dormant Script Injection Capability
articles.summary: A widely-used Chrome extension called Adblock for YouTube, with over 10 million installations, was discovered to contain hidden code capable of executing arbitrary JavaScript on users' browsers. This finding highlights how popular browser extensions can pose significant security risks even when they seem trustworthy.
articles.whyItMatters: Browser extensions with millions of users represent a critical attack surface because they operate with elevated privileges and can access sensitive user data, browsing history, and credentials. articles.title: ThreatsDay Bulletin: Smart TV Proxyware, 24-Year curl Bug, AI Crime Forums + 13 More Stories
articles.summary: This week's cybersecurity bulletin covers multiple emerging threats including smart TV proxyware, a critical 24-year-old curl vulnerability, and AI-powered crime forums. articles.title: Surviving the Mythos Era: Richard Bejtlich on the Case for NDR

Network Detection and Response (NDR) tools are presented as a solution to help teams understand the full scope of incidents with proper evidence and visibility.
articles.whyItMatters: This article addresses a critical gap in many SOCs where teams lack adequate visibility and context during incident response, leading to incomplete investigations and potential missed threats. articles.title: ShapedPlugin WordPress Pro Plugins Backdoored in Supply Chain Attack
articles.summary: Hackers successfully infiltrated ShapedPlugin's WordPress plugin distribution system, injecting malicious backdoor code into multiple Pro plugins. articles.title: Microsoft quietly extends free Windows 10 ESU support to October 2027
articles.summary: Microsoft has extended its free Extended Security Updates (ESU) program for Windows 10 consumers by an additional year, pushing the support deadline to October 12, 2027. articles.summary: Researchers have identified a new macOS malware called 'Gaslight' that uses deceptive techniques to evade AI-powered malware analysis tools. articles.title: PirloTV sports piracy network disrupted as 44 domains seized

articles.summary: A critical flaw in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN (CVE-2026-20245) was actively exploited by unknown attackers months before Cisco publicly disclosed it. articles.title: Dawn of the Apex Agentic Adversary
articles.summary: The cybersecurity landscape is fundamentally shifting from human-paced threat cycles to rapid, automated attacks powered by advanced AI agents. articles.title: AutoJack Attack Lets One Web Page Hijack AI Agent for Host Code Execution
articles.summary: Researchers at Microsoft have discovered an exploit called AutoJack that allows attackers to compromise AI browsing agents and use them to execute malicious code on a user's computer. By tricking an AI agent into visiting a malicious webpage, attackers can run JavaScript that communicates with local services and launches programs on the host system without requiring user credentials or additional interaction. This attack chain transforms what should be a helpful AI tool into a backdoor for unauthorized code execution.
articles.whyItMatters: This vulnerability is critical because AI browsing agents are increasingly used in enterprise and consumer environments, and this exploit allows attackers to bypass traditional security controls without user awareness. articles.title: CISA warns of max severity Ubiquiti flaws exploited in attacks
articles.summary: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has issued a warning about maximum severity vulnerabilities in Ubiquiti UniFi OS and Lantronix serial-to-ethernet servers that are being actively exploited by attackers. These flaws pose an immediate threat to organizations using these networking devices. Administrators need to apply patches urgently to prevent unauthorized access and potential network compromise.
articles.whyItMatters: Active exploitation of maximum severity vulnerabilities in widely-used networking equipment means attackers are already compromising systems in the wild. Organizations running Ubiquiti and Lantronix devices must treat this as an immediate priority, as these devices often control critical network access points. articles.title: Amadey, StealC malware operations disrupted in Operation Endgame action
articles.summary: Microsoft, Europol, and international law enforcement partners have successfully disrupted the infrastructure supporting Amadey and StealC malware operations through Operation Endgame. This coordinated action targets the criminal services and infrastructure that enable ransomware gangs and other cybercriminals to conduct attacks. The operation represents a significant effort to dismantle malware distribution networks at a global scale.
articles.whyItMatters: This disruption demonstrates that coordinated international law enforcement can effectively target malware infrastructure, reducing the tools available to cybercriminals and ransomware operators. Organizations using systems compromised by Amadey or StealC may need to assess their security posture and implement additional protections now that these campaigns have been disrupted.

articles.title: Securing the service desk: Why social engineering attacks keep succeeding
articles.summary: Service desks have become prime targets for social engineering attacks, where threat actors manipulate helpdesk staff to gain unauthorized access to corporate systems, passwords, and multi-factor authentication settings. The article explains how these attacks work and provides defensive strategies that organizations can implement to protect their service desk operations from exploitation.
articles.whyItMatters: Service desks are often overlooked security weak points because attackers exploit human psychology rather than technical vulnerabilities, making them extremely effective entry points for account compromise. articles.title: Stealthy Mistic backdoor linked to ransomware access broker KongTuke
articles.summary: Researchers discovered a new backdoor called Mistic being used in targeted attacks against organizations in insurance, education, IT, and professional services. The backdoor has been linked to KongTuke, a known ransomware access broker who sells entry points to compromised networks. This stealthy malware allows attackers to establish persistent access before deploying ransomware or stealing data.
articles.whyItMatters: This threat demonstrates how attackers use specialized backdoors as a first step in sophisticated ransomware operations, making early detection critical for organizations in targeted sectors. articles.title: ‘Popa’ Botnet Linked to Publicly-Traded Israeli Firm
articles.summary: A massive Android botnet called Popa has been operating for four years, compromising millions of TV boxes to facilitate advertising fraud, account takeovers, and data scraping. Security researchers have connected the botnet to NetNut, a residential proxy service owned by Alarum Technologies, a publicly-traded Israeli company listed on NASDAQ. This discovery reveals how legitimate-looking companies may be involved in large-scale cybercriminal infrastructure.
articles.whyItMatters: This case demonstrates how botnets can operate at scale while concealed within established commercial services, making it harder for consumers to identify compromised devices and for law enforcement to disrupt operations.
